Content: Scientists are interested in determining the impact of the construction of a hydroelectric dam on a population of salmon that live downstream of a populated area. They measure the health of the salmon population in its current state, several `text(years)` after the dam was constructed. Which of the following would be the best to use as a control in this study?

A.Choice: The health of the salmon population in the river before humans lived in the area

B.Choice: The health of the salmon population at the apex of the dam's construction

C.Choice: The health of the salmon population just after the dam's construction was completed

D.Choice: The health of the salmon population prior to any dam construction

SubTopics: Describe the use of nuclear energy in power generation.
Content: Which of the following best describes the process of electricity generation at a nuclear power plant?

A.Choice: Nuclear power is generated through fission, which releases a large amount of heat. The heat is used to generate steam, which turns a turbine that powers a generator.

B.Choice: Nuclear power is generated when photons are converted to a direct current using a semiconducting material such as silicon. An inverter is used to convert the direct-current electricity into an alternating current.

C.Choice: Nuclear power is generated from the thermal energy of `text(Earth)`, which is a result of radioactive decay. The water underground is turned to steam, which turns a turbine to produce electricity.

D.Choice: Nuclear power is generated from the combustion of mined uranium, which provides enough heat to power a generator. The generator turns a turbine to create electricity.

SubTopics: Describe island biogeography.
Content: Scientists are interested in determining the average number of species that have migrated from the mainland to a group of islands, as shown below. Partway through their study, they decided to include an additional island in their study group.
problems/APES/media/14a.jpg

Based on the theory of island biogeography, which of the following best explains how the scientists' calculation of average number of species would change with the inclusion of this new island in their study?

A.Choice: The average would increase because more species would have migrated directly to the farther island.

B.Choice: The average would decrease because fewer species would have migrated directly to the farther island.

C.Choice: The average would not change because it is likely that the additional island has about the same number of species that migrated as the original island group.

D.Choice: The average would not change because the island is approximately the same size as those in the original group and therefore just as likely to recruit species from the mainland.

SubTopics: Describe the environmental changes and effects that result from El Niño or La Niña events (El Niño-Southern Oscillation).
Content: During an El Niño event, warm surface water moves from the western equatorial Pacific Ocean to the eastern equatorial region. Which of the following best describes how the warm water will affect upwelling off the coast of equatorial South America?

A.Choice: The warm surface water will not change upwelling because this region is at the equator and always has warm water.

B.Choice: The warm surface water will increase upwelling because of the difference in salinity between the warm surface water and the cold deep water.

C.Choice: The warm surface water will decrease upwelling because the cooler temperatures on land in the region will prevent upwelling.

D.Choice: The warm surface water will decrease upwelling because of the density difference between the warm surface water and the cold deep water.

Content: An individual has decided to convert a grassy area on property to a large garden in order to grow food, primarily vegetables. The garden measures `50` `text(meters)` in length by `7` `text(meters)` in width.
Describe one environmental advantage of producing food locally.
Vegetable production in the garden was less than expected for the season.

:ibox:i. Identify one soil property that affects crop production.

ii. The gardener applied a synthetic fertilizer to the garden for the next growing season. Describe one benefit of using synthetic fertilizer in the garden.

iii. A neighbor proposes using compost rather than a synthetic fertilizer on the garden, stating that composting is a more sustainable agricultural practice. Justify this claim.

The gardener finds a synthetic fertilizer with `34%` nitrogen and a recommended application rate of `1` `text(kg)` of nitrogen per `70.0` `text(square meters)`. Calculate the number of `text(kilograms)` of synthetic nitrogen fertilizer that should be spread on the garden area. Show your work.

The gardener also finds a local compost source with `2.5%` nitrogen. Calculate the number of `text(kilograms)` of compost that would need to be added to the garden to provide as much nitrogen as using the synthetic fertilizer. Show your work.

The price of a `text(kilogram)` of synthetic fertilizer is `$3.11`, while the price of a `text(kilogram)` of compost is `$0.04`. Calculate the savings, in `text(dollars)`, to provide `1` `text(kg)` of nitrogen per `70` `text(square meters)` using compost rather than nitrogen. Show your work.
